title: Parametric comma target-projection fibers with a specified target equivalence
statement:
Use the quasicategories, coherent transformations, functor simplicial sets, mapping spaces and homotopy fibers of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the canonical composition of mapping spaces of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Fix a universe containing all objects below. Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal D$ be arbitrary functors of quasicategories and let
$$E=\mathcal C\times_{F,\mathcal D,\mathrm{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal D)\times_{\mathrm{ev}_1,\mathcal D,G}\mathcal B,\qquad p:E\to\mathcal B.$$
For any simplicial set $K$ in this universe, there is a canonical simplicial isomorphism between $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$ and the same comma construction for $F_*:\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal D)$ and $G_*:\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal D)$. It respects both endpoint projections and commutes with restriction along every simplicial map $K'\to K$.
Let $a=(A,B,\alpha:FA\to GB)$ and $a'=(A',B',\alpha':FA'\to GB')$ be objects of this functor quasicategory, and let $\beta:B'\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ be a specified equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B)$. Set $\gamma=(G\beta)\alpha':FA'\to GB$. Define
$$q:\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)}(a,a')\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B)}(B,B),\qquad k\mapsto\beta\circ p(k),$$
$$\phi:\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(A,A')\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal D)}(FA,GB),\qquad h\mapsto\gamma\circ F(h).$$
Then there is an equivalence of homotopy fibers
$$\operatorname{hofib}_{\mathrm{id}_B}(q)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{\alpha}(\phi).$$
This comparison retains the specified transformation $\gamma=(G\beta)\alpha'$ and all higher homotopies; it is natural in these data and compatible with every restriction $K'\to K$. No universal-arrow property, adjunction, fullness, or fibration hypothesis on $F$ or $G$ is assumed.

proof.text: An $n$-simplex of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$ is a triple of maps $A_n:K\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal C$, $B_n:K\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal B$, and $w_n:K\times\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal D$, whose two restrictions are $FA_n$ and $GB_n$. An $n$-simplex of the comma construction for $F_*,G_*$ is exactly the same triple, after interchanging the factors $\Delta^n,\Delta^1$ in the last map. Interchanging them back is the inverse. Simplicial operators restrict the $\Delta^n$ coordinate, so the bijections give a simplicial isomorphism. The first two coordinates are unchanged. Precomposing the $K$ coordinate with $K'\to K$ commutes strictly with this interchange.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal C_K=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$, and similarly $\mathcal B_K,\mathcal D_K$. These are quasicategories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-comma-mapping-pullback] to $F_*:\mathcal C_K\to\mathcal D_K$ and $G_*:\mathcal B_K\to\mathcal D_K$; no fibration assumption on these functors is needed. Set $X=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C_K}(A,A')$, $Y=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B_K}(B,B')$, and $Z=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D_K}(FA,GB')$. Put $f(h)=\alpha'F(h)$ and $g(k)=G(k)\alpha$. The cited theorem gives a natural equivalence, over $Y$, from $M=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)}(a,a')$ to $P=X\times_Z^hY$. The projection to $Y$ is the actual target projection on mapping spaces. All these mapping spaces and path pullbacks are Kan; in particular the statement concerns spaces, including possibly empty ones.

proof.text: Put $Y_0=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B_K}(B,B)$ and $Z_0=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D_K}(FA,GB)$. Postcomposition gives $t:Y\to Y_0$, $t(k)=\beta k$, and $s:Z\to Z_0$, $s(z)=(G\beta)z$. Both are homotopy equivalences: choose inverse-triangle witnesses for $\beta$; their images under $G_*$ are inverse-triangle witnesses for $G\beta$. By associativity and unitality of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], postcomposition by these inverse edges supplies homotopy inverses of $t$ and $s$. This argument uses inverses only to verify equivalence, not to define the comparison. Define $v:Y_0\to Z_0$ by $v(l)=G(l)\alpha$. The same associativity gives specified homotopies $sf\simeq\phi$ and $sg\simeq vt$: explicitly, $(G\beta)(\alpha'F(h))\simeq((G\beta)\alpha')F(h)$ and $(G\beta)(G(k)\alpha)\simeq G(\beta k)\alpha$. For the compatibility with $G_*$, use [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality]: the induced mapping-space maps form a coherent natural transformation preserving the canonical composition and identity classes. Its naturality gives the homotopy between $G(\beta)G(k)$ and $G(\beta k)$ simultaneously on the parameter space, including further homotopies. Thus the first map is exactly composition with the required $\gamma=(G\beta)\alpha'$, rather than an independently chosen arrow.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-commuting-pullback-invariance] to the cospans $(X\xrightarrow f Z\xleftarrow gY)$ and $(X\xrightarrow\phi Z_0\xleftarrow vY_0)$ with vertex maps $1_X,s,t$ and the two homotopies just written. They are equivalences by Step 3, and all vertices are Kan by Step 2. We obtain an equivalence $P\simeq P_0=X\times_{Z_0}^hY_0$, whose second projection is $t\operatorname{pr}_Y$. In the path model it sends $(h,k,\lambda:f(h)\simeq g(k))$ to $(h,t(k),\lambda_0:\phi(h)\simeq v(t(k)))$, with $\lambda_0$ the image $s\lambda$ adjusted by those two endpoint homotopies. Composing with Step 2 gives an equivalence $M\simeq P_0$ over $Y_0$, with the commutation homotopy retained, and the map from $M$ is precisely $q$. Apply the same invariance theorem to the cospans $(M\xrightarrow qY_0\xleftarrow{\mathrm{id}_B}*)$ and $(P_0\xrightarrow{\operatorname{pr}_2}Y_0\xleftarrow{\mathrm{id}_B}*)$, with identity maps on the last two vertices. Hence $\operatorname{hofib}_{\mathrm{id}_B}(q)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{\mathrm{id}_B}(\operatorname{pr}_2)$.

proof.text:
The square $P_0\to X$ over $Y_0\xrightarrow v Z_0$ is the defining homotopy-pullback square. Pull it back along the point $\mathrm{id}_B:*\to Y_0$. By [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting], the resulting outer rectangle is a homotopy pullback, and so
$$\operatorname{hofib}_{\mathrm{id}_B}(\operatorname{pr}_2)\simeq X\times_{Z_0}^h\{v(\mathrm{id}_B)\}.$$
Unitality in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] supplies the path $v(\mathrm{id}_B)=G(\mathrm{id}_B)\alpha\simeq\alpha$; applying homotopy-commuting pullback invariance with identity vertex maps and this endpoint path identifies the last space with $\operatorname{hofib}_{\alpha}(\phi)$. Explicitly a point of the left fiber consists of $(h,l,\lambda_0:\phi(h)\simeq v(l),\rho:l\simeq\mathrm{id}_B)$; the comparison retains $h$ and concatenates $\lambda_0$, $v\rho$, and the unitality path to obtain a path from $\phi(h)$ to $\alpha$. Pasting proves this is an equivalence of the full spaces, rather than just a bijection of their components.

proof.text: The comparison is the one just described: a coherent comma square is postcomposed with the specified $G\beta$, and its target path under $\beta$ is then pasted to the identity. The comma mapping equivalence is natural in objects and cospan functors by [lem-coef-infinity-comma-mapping-pullback]; homotopy-commuting pullback invariance retains every parameter simplex and further homotopy; and pullback pasting uses exactly the concatenated commutation homotopy. Use [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality] for the coherent naturality of the pre/postcomposition maps and their unit and composition homotopies as objects, functors and transformations vary. Apply it in a sufficiently large pair of universes to the functor quasicategories in Step 2. Together with the parameter compatibility of the two path-pullback statements, these coherent natural transformations give a natural comparison retaining the arrow $\gamma$ from Step 3. For restriction, a simplicial map $r:K'\to K$ acts by precomposing every displayed simplex with $r\times1$. It carries $\alpha,\alpha',\beta$ and their composition triangles to the restricted data; the same Hom-bifunctor theorem supplies compatibility of the mapping-space operations with this restriction functor, with its coherent homotopies. The interchange in Step 1 commutes strictly with this operation. Thus each diagram of comparisons commutes with restriction with its induced coherent homotopies, and all higher homotopies remain present. No pointwise universal-arrow condition, adjunction or fullness was used.
